summary: The medium checkpoint served a browser demo through an SSH tunnel and passed health plus one real model step, but 7.4-second steady-step latency rejected the low-latency hypothesis.

observations.name: shutdown_timer_due
observations.policy: three-hour user evaluation window after verified readiness

deviations: The first demo process failed because ThreadPrefetchIterDataset was iterable but not an iterator; commit 58758e5 wrapped it with iter and restarted only the demo process.
The training and evaluation pipeline, selected checkpoint, and context metrics were not rerun or changed during demo recovery.

failures.message: Model selection and DSW availability were initially unresolved.

observed: The selected medium checkpoint loaded and GET /health passed remotely and through the local SSH tunnel.
POST /api/step executed real model inference and returned a generated PNG frame for action 7.
Warm-up took 24.0 seconds and the verified steady step took 7.4 seconds.
interpretation: The functional demo smoke test passed, but the low-latency hypothesis is rejected on this implementation and A10.
The interface is suitable for deliberate frame-by-frame inspection, not real-time game control.
not_established: Qualitative button-to-motion controllability across multiple actions.
Browser interaction quality under sustained autoregressive rollout.
decision: Expose http://127.0.0.1:7860 for the verified three-hour user window.
Treat latency optimization as a separate engineering experiment rather than claiming this is real time.

revision_history.reason: Backfilled planned demo protocol and dependency block.
Closed the recovered demo with remote and tunneled health, one real inference step, latency evidence, and a three-hour user window.
